input.description: Search for callers and error handling

input.reason: I read src/api.ts and its only caller, src/dashboard.ts. `fetchCurrentUser` (api.ts:11-14) passes its response to `json`, which throws when `!res.ok` (api.ts:7). `loadDashboard` (api.ts:26-30) awaits it without a try/catch, so a failed /api/me request rejects the dashboard load. The render callback never runs, and `mountDashboard` (dashboard.ts:4-7) stays on "Loading...", because it calls `void loadDashboard(...)` without a catch. `fetchUserList` (api.ts:16-24) is different. It wraps its request in try/catch and returns `[]` for a non-ok status or a thrown error, so it cannot reject the load. F01 holds as written. F03 is edited to name only `fetchCurrentUser` as the source of the rejection. The Summary said the page crashes, but the code only shows the page stuck on "Loading..." with an unhandled rejection, so I rewrote it.
input.summary: fetchCurrentUser failures reject loadDashboard and the dashboard never renders

findings.text: `fetchCurrentUser` rejects on any non-2xx status, and `loadDashboard` does not catch it.
findings.reason: Claim 1: `fetchCurrentUser` returns `json<User>(res)` (api.ts:13), and `json` throws `new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)` when `!res.ok` (api.ts:7). `res.ok` is false for every status outside 200-299, so any non-2xx response rejects. Claim 2: `loadDashboard` runs `const me = await fetchCurrentUser();` (api.ts:27) with no try/catch around it, so the rejection propagates. Its only caller, dashboard.ts:5, calls it as `void loadDashboard(...)` and does not catch either.

findings.text: `loadDashboard` awaits `fetchCurrentUser` and `fetchUserList` with no error handling. A failed request from `fetchCurrentUser` rejects the dashboard load, and the page never renders.
findings.reason: `loadDashboard` does await both functions with no try/catch (api.ts:27-28). A failure in `fetchCurrentUser` does reject the load, the `render` callback at api.ts:29 never runs, and dashboard.ts leaves the root showing "Loading...". The claim that a failure in either function rejects the load is wrong for `fetchUserList`. That function catches every error and returns `[]` for both a non-ok status and a thrown fetch, so it never rejects. I narrowed "either one" to `fetchCurrentUser`.

input.severity_reason: The bug only shows up when /api/me fails, such as on a 401 after a session expires or a server error. The dashboard then stays on "Loading..." with an unhandled promise rejection. The page does not crash and no data is lost, so this is wrong behavior on an error path rather than a common one.
